summary: Sporting News' Week 10 fantasy football injury report covers the status of four injured pass-catchers: Justin Jefferson, Ja'Marr Chase, T.J. Hockenson and Curtis Samuel. Jefferson was ruled out, while Chase, Hockenson and Samuel were officially active. The article gives fantasy advice for each player and notes that Tee Higgins and Nico Collins are out.
one_line: Week 10 fantasy injury updates: Jefferson is out, while Chase, Hockenson and Samuel are active, with start/sit advice for each.
key_facts: Justin Jefferson (hamstring) was officially ruled OUT for the Vikings' Week 10 game against the Saints, according to NFL Network's Tom Pelissero; he would have needed activation by 4 p.m. ET Saturday.
Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said earlier in the week it would be "a little aggressive" for Jefferson to return this week; Jefferson had three straight limited practices.
With Jefferson out, Josh Dobbs is under center for Minnesota instead of Kirk Cousins; K.J. Osborn (concussion) was questionable after going from DNP Wednesday to full practice Friday.
If Jefferson is out but Osborn returns, both Osborn and Jordan Addison are worth using in fantasy.
Ja'Marr Chase (back) was officially ACTIVE for the Bengals' 1 p.m. ET home game against the Texans after a pre-game workout; he was a DNP Wednesday, then logged back-to-back limited practices.
Tee Higgins (hamstring) and Nico Collins were already ruled OUT for Week 10; the Bengals will also be without edge rusher Sam Hubbard.
If Chase were out, Tyler Boyd would be a must-start, with Trenton Irwin and Andrei Iosivas as secondary options in deep leagues; Joe Burrow appears finally healthy.
T.J. Hockenson (ribs) was listed questionable but officially ACTIVE against New Orleans, per Ian Rapoport's report that he was expected to play.
Hockenson has not missed a game this season despite injury woes, and leads the Vikings in targets with 80; he is not benched in any fantasy format.
Dobbs enjoyed targeting tight ends in Arizona and continued that in his Minnesota debut.
Curtis Samuel (toe) was officially ACTIVE for the Commanders' 4:25 p.m. ET game against the Seahawks; the toe injury dates to Week 8's game against the Eagles.
Sporting News advises against starting Samuel unless in a bind, since his workload is unclear; Jamison Crowder emerged in his absence and Jahan Dotson's production has increased.
